items_missed: No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned once in 43 minutes — and the customer's single loudest objection was damage from multiple handling: 'that's four handling and you know most of it does beat up enough and I was trying to avoid that.' The $2,000 coverage was the direct answer to his stated fear and it never came up.

Meet Your Mover never mentioned — the customer explicitly raised crew continuity: 'I know that you guys have different crews may not even get the same guys out here.' Textbook Meet Your Mover moment, missed.

No 'pricing is super simple' framing and no no-hidden-fees pitch. Instead the pricing came out as a raw number stream; the customer said 'there's a whole lot of numbers' and 'Wow! This is escalating fast.'
No deposit required never mentioned. Worse, the only deposit language in the call was the $12-per-blanket pad deposit, which for a cash-conscious customer reads as 'there is a deposit.'
No day-of-week rate tiers explained despite quoting two different branch rates ($97/hr Fort Worth, $103/hr) on two different dates.

Save Your Ass speech never delivered. He conceded the principle reactively — 'anything you do beforehand certainly helps to trim down the time' — only after the customer volunteered his own prep. Zero consolidation examples, zero carload tip (the customer supplied that himself), no 'does that make sense?' close.

Never asked for the booking. Closed passively: 'if you wanted to move forward you can just respond directly to that email.' He had confirmed availability on both dates and never converted that into an ask.
Never asked the customer to reply and verify details, never mentioned a bolded detail list at the top of the email, never gave business hours.
Customer's name mangled the entire call — 'even', 'VIN', 'fence', 'Vance pump free' — and never used correctly or confirmed, even after the customer said 'everyone spelled it wrong.'

Email address never read back or confirmed. The customer said 'I don't know if I gave my email address or not.' The one deliverable of this call is an emailed estimate to an unverified address on a misspelled name.
No box count ever pinned down on a move where box volume drives the one-truck-vs-two-truck decision — customer said 'a million boxes', 'another four wardrobes', plus an attic full.
No access, parking, or walk-distance questions at either address, and none at the storage unit — nor pod placement, despite pods being the live alternative.
Destination square footage never obtained ('it's way bigger', 'huge') on a home he was estimating a crew size for.
No stressor question asked — the customer volunteered his concerns unprompted.
No equivalents used (school bus or similar) in a call that was drowning the customer in raw numbers.
Traffic never mentioned as a variable on a 57-mile Denton-to-Arlington leg.
No sense-check anywhere in the clock or pricing explanation, despite two explicit overload signals from the customer.
No Ecobox referral (customer needs four-plus more wardrobe boxes) and no Sparefoot referral (customer actively shopping third-party and climate-controlled storage).
No 60 cents/lb insurance baseline — no insurance explanation of any kind.
Sat in silence for four minutes watching the walkthrough video with the customer live on the line rather than offering to call back.
top_strength: The estimating and the honesty were excellent, and the customer said so: 'I appreciate your honesty and upfront' and 'the first people to actually give me a quote.' Khevan watched the walkthrough video on the spot, then modeled the job four different ways — two-day storage split, pods labor-only, and same-day if the lease-back came through — and justified crew size against real items he had seen ('I saw the grandfather clock in there, patio stuff, garage stuff'). He explained the estimating method transparently (square footage first, video refines it), that they only bill time used, the 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, and the $115-per-truck zone fee in both directions with the reasoning behind it. Best moment was building a live budget-protection plan on the fly: 'at about an hour and a half two hours of loading, do a quick little time check' with milestone checks to hold the $3,600 target. He also right-sized down from five movers to three to protect the customer's wallet, and his 'I can sit in silence for four minutes if you'd like' got real rapport going.
coaching_note: Khevan, this call had the best estimating I have graded and it still scored 47, because the three differentiators that answer this exact customer's objections never came out of your mouth. Highest-leverage fix: when he said 'that's four handling and most of it does beat up enough and I was trying to avoid that,' that is No Worries and Meet Your Mover, back to back — 'Vance, that concern is exactly why we carry No Worries Damage Coverage, up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse, and every piece bigger than a microwave gets blanketed and shrink-wrapped before it moves. And a few days out you'll get an email with your movers' photos and info, so you know who's handling it — and since you're on both ends of a storage job, we'll aim to keep the same crew.' That answers damage and crew continuity, the two things he actually cared about, and neither costs a dollar off the quote. Second priority: sequence the pricing instead of streaming it. He told you twice he was drowning — 'whole lot of numbers', 'escalating fast' — so lead with 'pricing is super simple', give him one option at a time, land the no-hidden-fees list and no deposit required, and sense-check with 'does that make sense so far?' before the next number. Third, you never asked for the business: you had confirmed availability on both dates and closed with 'respond to that email.' Say 'both those days are open right now, there's no deposit, so I can hold them for you today.' BUSINESS RISK, three items. One, you told a customer our state-required contract maximum is 'typically two and a half times the estimate' — please verify that figure against the actual contract terms, because that is a binding number you just quoted out loud. Two, no EMMA profile existed at the time of this call and you verbally quoted at least four configurations ($3,600 plus $2,400 two-part, $2,860.50 pods, $2,752 same-day, on top of Zachary's earlier $3,600) to a customer who told you 'I wrote down the stuff as he was talking' — high risk the written estimate does not match what he has on his notepad. Three, you quoted Fort Worth rates and availability from the McKinney office on a job you determined Fort Worth should service; confirm Fort Worth can honor $97/hr on 9/9 and $103/hr on 9/19 before the estimate goes out. And his email address was never confirmed on a misspelled name, so the estimate may never arrive.
phone_presence_notes: Genuinely warm and unusually honest — the humor landed, he let the customer talk, he validated the pods option against his own interest, and the customer stayed positive through $6,000 of sticker shock and asked how to reach him again; held back from a 5 only by never once getting or using the customer's name correctly.
